groundings.excerpt:
213: Let $\Lambda=\Lambda(x_1,x_2,\ldots)$ be the ring of symmetric functions with integral coefficients. This space has a ${\mathbb Z}$-linear basis consisting of \emph{Schur functions} $s_{\lambda}$,
214: where $\lambda$ is an integer partition. Consider the ideal
215: \[I_{r,n-r} = \mathrm{Span}_\mathbb{Z}\left\{s_\lambda\mid \lambda\nsubseteq (n-r)^r \right\} \]
216: of $\Lambda$. Then one has the following standard presentation of the cohomology of Grassmannians:
217: \[H^*(\mathrm{Gr}_{r,n})\cong \Lambda/I_{r,n-r}. \]
218: We will use an overline to denote the projection $\Lambda\to\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}$. Specifically, we will write $\overline{\Lambda}$ as a shorthand for $\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}$. We will also distinguish between $s_{\lambda}\in \Lambda$, the usual Schur function, and $\overline{s}_{\lambda}$ for its image in $\overline{\Lambda}$.

claims.text: With \(A_+:=\bigoplus_{e>0}A_e\) and \(\bar h_t=\bar s_{(t)}\), one has \(A_+=(\bar h_1,\ldots,\bar h_5)\).

Put \[ C_d=\{\mu:22\subseteq\mu\subseteq5^6,\ |\mu|=d\},\qquad R_d=\{(t,\lambda):1\le t\le5,\ 22\subseteq\lambda\subseteq5^6,\ |\lambda|=d-t\}. \] The row indexed by \((t,\lambda)\in R_d\), in the basis \(C_d\), is \[ \bar h_t\bar s_\lambda =\sum_{\substack{\mu\in C_d\\\mu/\lambda\text{ horizontal }t\text{-strip}}}\bar s_\mu, \] and the lattice spanned by all these rows is exactly \((A_+J)_d\).

\(R_d=\varnothing\) for \(d\le4\) (hence for \(d<4\)) and for \(d>35\). For every \(31\le d\le35\), \(R_d\ne\varnothing\), since \((d-30,5^6)\in R_d\), but every indexed row is the zero vector because \(C_d=\varnothing\).
